query: An equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy has a simple solid-solution structure and favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength, while its microstructure and deformation behavior remain insufficiently understood. Under hardness testing and mechanical loading of this starting state, what single intervention could overcome the strength and hardness limitation while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics? State the proposed intervention, its mechanism, the predicted measurable change relative to the unmodified alloy, its applicable processing and test conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a microstructural and mechanical experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Intervention of adding a small amount of alloying elements such as Al, Cu, or Mn to the equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with simple solid-solution structure
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of alloying elements such as Al, Cu, or Mn
generation.mechanism: Precipitation or clustering of alloying elements leading to increased strength and hardness
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased strength and hardness while retaining favorable mechanical characteristics
generation.boundary: Applicable processing and test conditions include varying temperatures, strain rates, and loading modes
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the optimal amount and type of alloying elements to add
generation.falsification_experiment: Microstructural and mechanical characterization of the modified alloy under various processing and test conditions
